message.content:
For a single flip of a fair coin, there are two equally likely outcomes: heads or tails.  
The probability of obtaining heads is therefore  

\[
P(\text{heads})=\frac{\text{number of favorable outcomes}}{\text{total possible outcomes}}
               =\frac{1}{2}=0.5 \quad (\text{or } 50\%).
\]

This assumes the coin is unbiased and each flip is independent.
